newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu ends down at 5,300/400 vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu ends down at 5,300/400 vs dlr.

text.p: Romania's leu currency fell further on Friday, closing at 5,300/400 to the dollar after it lost some five percent in early trade on an interbank market suffering chronic hard currency shortages.

The leu lost 23.7 percent against the dollar this week, its sharpest weekly fall in one year, and seemed headed for further decline, as market operators seek what could be considered a more realistic value amid renewed inflationary fears.
Traders said the market was unmoved by latest statistics showing a surge in inflation to a year-on-year 56.9 percent last year against 27.8 percent in 1995.
"This market cannot react swiftly to economic news. We had anticipated that inflation was on the rise, and the leu was overvalued," said one trader.

Operators said plans to liberalise the foreign exchange market in coming months had failed to impress the interbank market, which the former government restricted to only four market-making dealer banks last March.
Traders said the leu's downswing might end after reaching 5,500 to the dollar, which might be a "resistance level" for the sagging currency.
The leu's retail prices marked time at 5,700 to the dollar after gaining over the past week amid leu shortages at licensed money changing bureaux.
Traders said money market short-term rates were flat. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
